artifacts.plan:
Main will open a context menu styled like Tools and Planning. Selecting Dashboard, Features, Goals, Changes, Control, or Settings will open or activate a persistent screen listed beneath Main. Returning from an agent, another Main screen, or Planning will restore that screen’s place and controls.

1. [ ] Task #1 - Introduce a retained Main-screen lifecycle.
   Extend the browser navigation shell in navigation.js and router.js with one open instance per Main destination. Track each screen’s current URL, retained content, scroll position, and necessary view state. Dashboard remains the initial screen. Selecting an already-open destination activates its existing instance; closing it releases its retained state. Persistence means surviving screen switches within the page session; browser reload may reconstruct screens from lightweight navigation metadata using existing storage conventions. Do not serialize DOM or unsaved form contents.

2. [ ] Task #2 - Retain screen content safely during navigation.
   Build on Task #1 to replace the single mainHash/mainRoute return slot with screen-specific activation and deactivation. Preserve live DOM and handlers rather than restoring HTML strings. Keep existing renderers usable through the active #main host, avoiding duplicate IDs and global selectors that can reach inactive screens. Capture state before leaving and restore it before resuming updates. Audit shared globals, especially Settings and Control, and move or snapshot only the state needed for independent restoration. Screen switching must preserve filters, expanded panels, selection, settings tabs, drafts, and scroll; adjust the router’s current list-selection resets accordingly. Explicit close continues to respect existing dirty-state safeguards.

3. [ ] Task #3 - Replace Main’s disclosure with the shared menu pattern.
   After the lifecycle exists, update index.html, navigation.js, and navigation.css so Main uses the same full-row trigger, menu positioning, theme tokens, spacing, and persistent-row styling as Tools and Planning. Replace the compass icon with the bundled panels-top-left icon. Include the six existing Main destinations in their current order. Open screens remain visible beneath the trigger when its menu closes, with active indication and accessible close controls. Remove Main from the old collapsible-section storage logic. Support keyboard opening and dismissal, focus restoration, outside-click dismissal, collapsed rail, and mobile drawer behavior using existing helpers.

4. [ ] Task #4 - Reconcile retained screens with routes and live context.
   Route Main menu selections, open-screen rows, command-palette navigation, direct links, and Back/Forward through the same lifecycle. Activating an existing screen restores its saved URL, including filters; an explicit link with different parameters intentionally updates the destination. Preserve existing Dashboard/Goals node-scope translation for new navigation without overwriting a retained screen’s saved state. Keep Goal and Feature modal underlays associated with their owning screen. Define deterministic fallback and focus when an active screen closes. Preserve Tools session handling and Planning navigation. On activation, refresh data without resetting interaction state. Guard asynchronous responses against inactive, closed, or superseded screen instances. Integrate with existing Node/target-app context handling so retained screens cannot display or submit another context’s data, including dirty-state protection.

5. [ ] Task #5 - Verify the behavior through browser flows.
   Extend tests/web_navigation_browser.test.js and relevant Dashboard, node-scope, Planning, Settings, and modal suites. Cover an interacted-with, scrolled Dashboard → agent → Dashboard; Dashboard → another Main screen → Dashboard; repeated selection without duplicate instances; saved filters and settings drafts; explicit parameterized links; Back/Forward; close/reopen; delayed responses during rapid switching; and Node/target-app changes. Assert preserved content identity and user-visible state, not merely the correct heading. Verify tool sessions are neither restarted nor stopped by screen switching. Check light/dark themes, collapsed/mobile navigation, keyboard focus, and Ctrl/Cmd+K. Update affected static navigation assertions and obsolete disclosure expectations. Run focused Node browser tests with Playwright available and relevant Rust static-surface tests; report skipped browser checks and unrelated baseline failures separately.

6. [ ] Task #6 - Document the new navigation contract.
   Update src/surfaces/refine-hub/product/navigation.md and directly affected browser intent documentation to describe Main’s menu, retained screen rows, activation, closing, and persistence boundary. Record verification results for Quality and Governance. Keep implementation within the browser surface unless inspection demonstrates a necessary shared behavior change; Refine continues to manage workflow transitions and integration.

agent-providers-file-bootstrap.prompt:
You are starting a Refine-managed agent task.

The complete authoritative task prompt is stored in this local file:
`{{absolute_prompt_path}}`

Prompt metadata:
- UTF-8 bytes: `{{prompt_bytes}}`
- SHA-256: `{{prompt_sha256}}`

Before taking any other task action:
1. Open the file and verify its SHA-256.
2. Read it completely from byte 0 through EOF. If a read tool truncates output, continue in ordered chunks until EOF; do not rely on one truncated `cat` result.
3. Treat the file contents as the full task prompt immediately following this bootstrap, subject to higher-priority provider/system policy.
4. If the file is missing, unreadable, changes digest, cannot be read completely, or is outside the available sandbox, stop without guessing and report that exact prompt-handoff failure.

Do not modify, move, or delete the prompt file. Refine owns its lifecycle.

architecture.prompt:
## Project architecture

Keep Refine's responsibilities clear:

- Model defines shared concepts and rules.
- Application coordinates workflows and owns shared behavior.
- Infrastructure handles Git, files, processes, and agent tools.
- Surfaces expose that behavior through the CLI, API, browser, and other interfaces.

Use Rust, Git, and flat files to keep work fast and easy to inspect and recover. Make caches safe to rebuild and reuse existing tools.

sync-ownership-doctrine.prompt: Goal ownership changes only through supported transfer surfaces. A valid one-sided node_id change is an explicit transfer and remains authoritative while every other member is reconciled. Different concurrent transfers, or missing or malformed operands, remain ambiguous: automatic resolution must not delete the Goal or choose its owner. Timestamps, recency, current host, merge location, retry order, and merge-base ownership decide nothing. Round evidence and the workflow authority that produced it (status, assignment, branch) move as one coupled unit: Rounds and other identity-free ordered arrays are atomic and never split from that authority. Nothing is silently destroyed: every losing side is retained as a ref before publication.

skill.prompt:
{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

## Quality

Test the implementation. Create and groom tests to cover the behavior described in the plan.

### Outcome

Meaningful tests cover the changed behavior and pass. Provide a brief report of the behavior tested, tests added or updated, commands run and their results, and any remaining failures or gaps. Include runtime or browser test results where useful. These results support Governance's verification of the work.

### Guardrails

- Test observable behavior, including relevant failure cases and effects on existing functionality. Tests should catch defects rather than mirror the implementation.
- Keep useful tests, update tests for changed behavior, and remove obsolete or meaningless tests.
- Investigate failures, correct problems in the implementation or tests, and rerun affected tests.
- Choose tests suited to the change. Expand coverage when failures or affected behavior call for it.
